title: About Ni Haixia
life: Ni Haixia (1954–2012) was born in Taipei. As a young man he studied acupuncture with Dr. Zhou Zuoyu, and he called himself a modern heir to the Jingfang (classical formula) school, the tradition of the Shanghan lun (Treatise on Cold Damage). In 1991 he moved to the United States, where he was licensed in acupuncture in Florida and opened the Hantang clinic of Chinese medicine; in 1995 he founded the Hantang College of Chinese Medicine, and from then on he taught Chinese medicine and the traditional divination arts. He died in Taipei on January 31, 2012, at the age of 58.
teaching: Ni Haixia organized everything he had learned into two public teaching series. Ren Ji covers the Zhenjiu dacheng (Great Compendium of Acupuncture and Moxibustion), the Shennong bencao jing (Divine Farmer’s Classic of Materia Medica), the Huangdi neijing (Inner Classic of the Yellow Emperor), the Shanghan lun (Treatise on Cold Damage) and the Jingui yaolüe (Essentials from the Golden Cabinet). It is the “principles of humankind,” a complete path for learning Chinese medicine. Tian Ji covers Ziwei Doushu and the Yijing (Book of Changes). It is the “principles of heaven,” his systematic work on the divination arts.
approach: Ni Haixia was against memorizing formulas by rote; he put understanding the principles and sound logic first. This attitude helped Ziwei Doushu move from secrets handed down from teacher to student toward knowledge anyone can study systematically.
